issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about the type of the Farm.animals collection: the UML diagram shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual Part 3 explicitly requires using a Set implemented as a HashSet. The provided reference solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList), and the template Farm.java does not initialize any collection. This inconsistency will confuse students about whether to use a List or a Set (and whether uniqueness should be enforced) and leads to a mismatch between the textual requirements and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across the specification, template, and solution. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML and textual description to specify a List (and adjust wording about uniqueness), then modify the template to include a List (ArrayList) and keep the solution as-is; or (B) Adopt the textual requirement and change the UML to show Set<Animal>, then update the solution and template to use a Set (e.g., HashSet) with a no-arg constructor initializing the HashSet and ensure addAnimal/enforcement of uniqueness behaves accordingly. Ensure all artifacts (UML, textual description, template, and solution) match the chosen collection type.

issues.description: The representation of the Farm's collection of animals is inconsistent across artifacts: the UML in the problem statement declares animals as List<Animal>, the textual Part 3 instructions explicitly require a Set implemented with a HashSet, and the solution implements a List backed by an ArrayList. This mismatch creates confusion about the intended collection type and its semantics (uniqueness of animals) and could mislead students about which data structure to use and which behavior (allowing duplicates vs enforcing uniqueness) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across all artifacts. Prefer updating the solution and template to use Set<Animal> animals and initialize it with new HashSet<>() in the no-argument constructor (and update the UML to show Set<Animal>). Alternatively, if List is intended, update the textual instruction in Part 3 to request a List/ArrayList. The recommended fix to match the explicit requirement is: declare private Set<Animal> animals; initialize this.animals = new HashSet<>(); and adjust getters/setters and documentation accordingly.
